newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila calls for common APEC ground amid diversity.
newsitem.headline: Manila calls for common APEC ground amid diversity.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos urged APEC finance ministers on Saturday to immediately forge common strategies allowing freer flow of capital funds, despite the reservations of some east Asian economies.
"The work of bridge-building starts with the realisation that differences -- no less than similarities -- give rise to opportunities...which lead to consensus and cooperation.
"In our region, some differences represent strengths and open the door toward reform," Ramos said during the opening ceremonies of the fourth APEC finance ministers' meeting.

Finance ministers of APEC's 18 members are meeting at a luxury hotel here over the weekend to discuss ways to develop capital markets to help finance the $1.5 trillion infrastructure needs of the region over the next 10 years.
Assessments regarding the pace of the negotiations were mixed, with some delegates saying certain Asian economies were not too keen on liberalising capital markets in the near future.

Asian Development Bank director Paul Dickie, who helped deputy ministers draft the meeting's talking points, said on Friday that some east Asian economies were still wary over bad experiences in Latin America after countries there allowed freer access of foreign funds into their systems.
Ramos said he did not expect a rigid set of standards to be set up by all APEC nations, but said consensus was strongly needed in order to move forward.

"In APEC, we do not create unity by hammering one kind of system to be imposed from above for all, but by building bridges among our countries through consensual policy dialogue and adoption of common programmes," he said.
"It is easy enough to see the urgency of the tasks before us. It is harder to act upon them... There's a bridge to build, and we can start to build it now," he added.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
